Mr. Dipak Daga (0:20): 
Good evening, everyone.  
It gives me immense pleasure to welcome all of you to the Q2 FY27 earnings 
conference call of Jio Financial Services Limited. My name is Dipak Daga and I am 
the Group Chief Strategy Officer and Chief Investor Relations Officer of Jio Financial 
Services.  
On the call with us today, we have Mr. Hitesh Sethia, Managing Director and Chief 
Executive Officer of Jio Financial Services Limited, who will take us through the 
Company’s overall financial performance during the quarter and six months ended 
September 30, 2026.  
We are also joined by Mr. Ganesh A R, Group Executive and Chief Technology 
Officer who will take us through our Data and AI initiatives, along with the operating 
performance of our Lending and Payments businesses.  
We are also joined by Ms. Annapoorna Venkatramanan, Group Executive and Chief 
Financial Officer who will then walk us through the operating performance of our 
Investments and Insurance businesses, followed by the financial performance of Jio 
Financial Services Limited. 
1 

 
 
The earnings presentation for the quarter has been uploaded on our website, 
www.jfs.in, as well as on the stock exchanges. I would like to remind all participants 
that this call will be conducted in a listen-only mode.  
Before I hand over the call, I would like to read out the Safe Harbor statement. This 
presentation contains forward-looking statements which may be identified by their 
use of words like plans, expects, estimates or other words of similar meaning. All 
statements that address expectations or predictions about the future, including, but 
not limited to, statements about strategy for growth, product development, market 
position are forward statements based on rationale and data. Actual results may vary 
materially given the market circumstances.  
I will now hand over the call to Hitesh to discuss our business in detail.  
Mr. Hitesh Sethia (2:16): 
Thank you Dipak. 
Good evening, everyone. Season’s greetings and a very warm welcome to our 
earnings conference call for the second quarter of fiscal 2027. 
During Q2 FY27, we made further progress towards our goal of bringing new-age, 
hyper-personalised financial services to the people of India. Our objective of bringing 
in truly customer-centric innovation to financial services was evident this quarter 
through some industry-first initiatives that were rolled out on the JioFinance app, 
which will redefine the way people experience and engage with their finances.   
This period was also marked by the further scale-up of our businesses, expansion of 
our pan-India, omnichannel distribution network, and significant developments in our 
strategy of bringing world-class financial services to India, in collaboration with 
marquee global partners.  
Our business performance for the quarter reflects strong operational velocity across 
all our business lines, with our core operations continuing to build scale and drive 
performance across verticals.  
In our lending business, Jio Credit‘s Gross Assets Under Management rose to Rs. 
37,320 crore as of September 30, 2026, representing a 154% year-on-year growth 
and a steady sequential expansion over Q1 FY27. 
In payments, Jio Payments Bank expanded its customer deposit base to Rs. 643 
crore, up 53% year-on-year across 40 lakh CASA accounts. At Jio Payment 
Solutions, Total Payment Value, or TPV, stood at Rs. 14,682 crore. The 
quarter-on-quarter adjustment in TPV was a deliberate outcome of our strategic pivot 
2 

 
 
towards margin-accretive merchant segments. While this focus led to planned 
customer churn in lower-margin segments, it helped us realise higher net processing 
margins, giving us a base to grow volumes further with strong unit economics. 
In asset management, JioBlackRock AMC saw its Closing AUM reach Rs. 22,746 
crore, growing 57% year-on-year and 24% sequentially.  
In insurance broking, Jio Insurance Broking Limited facilitated total premiums of Rs. 
346 crore. 
Our reinsurance business, Allianz Jio Reinsurance Limited underwrote Rs. 244 crore 
in Gross Written Premium. This sequential moderation was driven by primary 
insurers recalibrating their exposure on account of crop insurance to align with 
current seasonal and environmental factors. 
This broad-based performance underscores our strategic focus on driving 
disciplined, quality-led expansion while building operating leverage across our 
full-stack financial ecosystem. 
Our financial performance during the second quarter and the first half of Fiscal Year 
2027 reflects our consistent operational strength across our core operating 
businesses. 
As we had highlighted during our Q1 FY27 earnings call, a key accounting change 
effected this financial year is the full consolidation of Reliance Services and Holdings 
Limited, or RSHL, as a 100% step-down subsidiary of the company, through 
Reliance Industrial Investments and Holdings Limited, or RIIHL. This was with effect 
from April 29, 2026 and consequently, RSHL's financials are now consolidated on a 
line-by-line basis with the company.  
It is also pertinent to point out JFS receives dividends each year, including from 
Reliance Industries Limited on account of its shareholding in the company, held 
through RIIHL and RSHL. In the fiscal year ended March 2026, this dividend was 
paid in the second quarter; whereas in the current fiscal, this dividend was paid in 
the first quarter.  
Excluding the impact of dividend in Q2 FY26, Consolidated Total Income grew 132% 
year-on-year to Rs. 1,699 crore for Q2 FY27; Pre-Provisioning Operating Profit 
reached Rs. 574 crore, registering a 85% growth year-on-year.  
Consolidated Profit Before Tax, excluding this dividend impact, increased 51% 
year-on-year to Rs. 489 crore for the quarter. Profit after tax for the quarter stood at 
Rs. 340 crore.   
3 

 
 
For the six months ended September 2026, excluding dividend, Consolidated Total 
Income increased 136% year-on-year to Rs. 3,195 crore; Pre-provisioning operating 
profit was up 60% year-on-year to Rs. 1,079 crore; and Consolidated profit before 
tax increased to Rs. 951 crore, up 33% year-on-year. Profit after tax for this period 
stood at Rs. 1,171 crore.   
Crucially, our core operating entities continue to anchor our overall performance. Led 
by an expanding loan book, Jio Credit Limited saw Q2 Profit After Tax jump 140% 
year-on-year to Rs. 120 crore. Simultaneously, we are making targeted investments 
to scale our growth-stage companies and incubate nascent ventures across asset 
management, wealth, and insurance. 
Our capital foundation remains robust with Total Consolidated Shareholders' Equity 
standing at Rs. 1.3 lakh crore as of September 30, 2026. This capital strength 
provides us with significant firepower to pursue our growth aspirations while keeping 
our core capital base fully protected. 
The company achieved a few strategic milestones in Q2 FY27, which demonstrate 
our sharp focus on execution, reinforcing our ability to scale sustainably while 
deepening customer engagement.  
The JioFinance app, our primary digital storefront for our retail offerings, clocked 3.2 
crore unique users across all digital properties, serving as the core engine for user 
acquisition and cross-sell.  
With our new neural agentic marketplace, we are endeavoring to usher in a new 
paradigm in the financial services by creating a platform that makes engagement 
with financial services more rewarding – both in terms of tangible benefits as well as 
towards improving the holistic financial well-being of our users.         
Towards this end, we unveiled two new pioneering features during the quarter to 
make finance smarter and more rewarding: 
First, JioFinance+, a first-of-its-kind value-back membership program that shares a 
portion of the platform commissions directly with the customers as tangible benefits 
on eligible transactions. This helps bring down transaction costs for the 
end-customer and empowers greater engagement.  
Second, JioFinance360, an industry-first proposition that consolidates multi-source 
asset and liability data into a single, comprehensive report, anchored by a Financial 
Health Score across five core pillars. 
The details of these two new features are covered in more detail in the subsequent 
sections.  
4 

 
 
In our lending vertical, we struck a landmark partnership during the quarter with Bank 
of America agreeing to acquire a 49.9% stake in Jio Credit. The transaction, which is 
subject to regulatory approvals, is expected to bring around Rs. 18,000 crore in 
growth capital.  
In our investment vertical, JioBlackRock Asset Management broadened its product 
line across five categories… across categories, while JioBlackRock Broking went live 
with its self-directed investing platform, featuring an introductory zero-brokerage 
structure across stocks, ETFs, and IPOs. 
To contextualize our progress, I want to emphasize our overarching objective: 
building a full-stack financial services institution anchored by dedicated operating 
entities across the four pillars of Borrow, Invest, Transact and Protect, with the 
JioFinance app serving as the central engine supporting the incubation and scale-up 
of these diverse businesses, which together form a virtuous flywheel of financial 
offerings designed to cater to the needs of all Indians.  
This full-stack franchise is anchored by five structural moats: our brand strength, a 
strong capital base, zero tech-debt, cost engineering at scale and a late entrant 
advantage, which allows us to observe and learn from evolving market dynamics and 
adapt with agility.  
Jio Financial Services now has the unique distinction of partnering with three of the 
world’s most well-regarded financial institutions - known for their pedigree and 
expertise in their respective area of operations: BlackRock for investments, Allianz 
for insurance and Bank of America for lending.   
From inception, we recognized that combining world-class product and operational 
expertise with our deep local reach creates a highly compelling value proposition. It 
brings globally recognised financial services experiences to our customers in India, 
and helps us build more resilient franchises by bringing in best-in-class governance, 
technology and risk management practices.   
Jio Financial Services retains full ownership of customer engagement and 
distribution, which helps us maintain superior unit economics and lower customer 
acquisition costs, and build a highly robust full-stack ecosystem.

The second layer introduces our marketplace aggregation framework. Recognizing 
that no single institution can fulfill every demographic's risk profile, we curate top-tier 
third-party offerings—like credit cards, personal loans, insurance, and fixed 
deposits—maximizing choice while maintaining strict risk discipline. 
Finally, the top layer represents our core pivot: an AI-native, conversational interface 
tailored for hyper-personalization of financial services to the level of each, unique 
individual user. Moving beyond static customer cohorts, our platform dynamically 
synthesizes real-time behavioral insights to recommend the exact right product for 
each individual's life stage—serving as an unbiased digital financial companion. 
Our distribution strategy is tailored specifically to the unique operational profile of 
each business line. High-frequency digital channels—namely the JioFinance app, 
MyJio, and our web portals—serve as our central digital storefronts, driving 
top-of-the-funnel customer acquisition across all entities.  
Where physical touchpoints are deployed, they are strategically calibrated to the 
specific requirements of the product segment. This omni-channel delivery footprint 
enables us to serve customers across more than 19,000 PIN codes in India. 
At Jio Credit Limited, where on-ground presence is required for physical verification 
and structured originations for mortgage loans, we have established 26 offices 
across 19 major cities. 
JioBlackRock Asset Management has proven the efficacy of our digital-first approach 
by successfully growing the overall segment as well as tapping the underpenetrated 
markets across the country. To further accelerate our growth trajectory, the AMC has 
established distribution partnerships with over 15,000 Distributors for Mutual funds 
and SIFs, combining digital reach with deep physical distribution.  
Jio Payments Bank has scaled its Business Correspondent network to over 633,000 
touchpoints, significantly deepening assisted digital banking access in semi-urban 
and rural centers. 
At Jio Payment Solutions, our merchant network spans 26 states, powered by 
AI-enabled merchant onboarding and automated deal negotiation tools. 
This fit-for-purpose distribution strategy ensures that as our product suite expands, 
our customer touchpoints remain highly accessible, operationally efficient, and 
cost-effective. 
I would like to invite our Group Executive and Chief Technology Officer, Mr. Ganesh 
A R to take you through our Data, Tech & AI initiatives, followed by updates on our 
NBFC and payments businesses.

Mr. Ganesh AR (15;36): 
Thank you Hitesh.  
Our investments in data, technology, and artificial intelligence are operationalizing 
deep structural capabilities across the group. 
As a digital-native organization built without legacy technology debt, our architecture 
is designed to integrate enterprise-wide intelligence directly into our workflows. This 
allows us to continuously optimize unit economics, improve process turnaround 
times, and scale our operating volume without a linear increase in cost structure. 
This slide illustrates the impact of our Data, Tech and AI initiatives across our four 
primary operational layers: Business Operations, Customer Experience, Risk & 
Fraud Management and Growth & Marketing.  
For instance, in Business Processes, Jio Credit has entirely digitised its debt 
collection and management process; whereas, Jio Payments Bank’s partner 
payment settlement process is now fully automated.   
In customer experience, our AI and machine learning models have driven 
hyper-personalized customer journeys on the JioFinance app, leading to a customer 
conversion rate uplift of 59%.  
And in terms of Growth and Marketing, data cohort-led campaigns drove a 172% 
improvement in conversion performance.  
These technology-led capabilities form the foundational bedrock as we drive 
execution across our core operating subsidiaries. 
Moving on to the performance of our lending entity, Jio Credit Limited. 
As we scale our lending franchise, our primary focus remains squarely on 
disciplined, risk-calibrated growth. We continue to build a high-quality loan book 
anchored entirely in secured lending segments and high-rated corporate exposures, 
ensuring that our growth is both sustainable and value-accretive. 
Gross Assets Under Management surged 154% year-on-year to reach Rs. 37,320 
crore, and up subsequent… sequentially from Rs. 30,667 crore in Q1 FY27. This 
sustained expansion in our loan book has been driven entirely by robust organic 
originations. 
7 

 
 
During the quarter, gross disbursements reached a new all time high of Rs. 13,135 
crore, representing a 98% year-on-year increase, and up from Rs. 11,252 crore in 
Q1 FY27. 
Our AUM mix remains well-balanced across our targeted borrowing cohorts. 
Mortgages, comprising Home Loans and Loan Against Property, account for 44.5% 
of the total portfolio, with an average ticket size of Rs. 1.4 crore and an average 
tenor of 15.9 years.  
Corporate and SME loans represent 44.2% of the book, with an average tenor of 
3.26 years, while retail Loan Against Securities accounts for 11.3%, carrying an 
average ticket size of Rs. 1.3 crore and an average tenor of 3 years. 
In terms of the disbursement mix for Q2 FY27, Mortgages contributed 26.1%, Loan 
Against Securities represented 20%, and Corporate and SME Loans accounted for 
53.9%. 
This prudent product diversification, coupled with our automated and digital-first 
underwriting frameworks, positions Jio Credit to capture market share, even as we 
continue to scale within risk management guardrails.  
Our liability strategy is built on maintaining a diversified, low-cost funding base 
backed by top-tier credit ratings and deep access to market liquidity. This enables us 
to maintain competitive product pricing while protecting our net interest margins. 
Looking at our borrowing trajectory for the quarter. 
Total borrowings stood at a little over Rs. 42,000 crore, representing a 250% 
year-on-year growth and up sequentially from Rs. 28,120 crore in Q1 FY27. This 
expansion directly supports the rapid scaling of our loan book. 
Our borrowing mix remains well-balanced across multiple debt instruments. Bank 
loans, including working capital demand loans and term loans, constitute around 
50% of our total borrowings, down from 60% in Q2 FY26. Additionally, cost efficient 
borrowing through TREPS were introduced during the quarter  
Our average cost of borrowing, excluding TREPS, stood at 7.08% in Q2 FY27, 
compared to 7.07% in Q1 FY27, demonstrating strong stability in a dynamic interest 
rate environment. 
On interest rate risk management, over 70% of our Assets Under Management are 
on floating rates, enabling interest rate adjustments to be seamlessly passed on to 
borrowers with minimal time lag.  
8 

 
 
Our capital position remains formidable. Total Shareholders' Equity stood at Rs. 
7,379 crore as of September 30, 2026, with a Capital Adequacy Ratio of 18.50%, 
providing comfortable headroom to support our future growth plans. The infusion of 
the first tranche of its investment of around Rs. 9,500 crore from Bank of America 
into Jio Credit Limited, subject to regulatory and statutory approvals, will further 
bolster our capital base and strengthen our balance sheet for long-term expansion.  
Looking at our financial performance for the second quarter. 
As our Assets Under Management continue to scale, the business is demonstrating 
strong operating leverage and scale-based cost efficiencies. 
Net Interest Income grew 116% year-on-year to Rs. 302 crore, and up sequentially 
from Rs. 257 crore in Q1 FY27. This growth reflects the expansion of our loan book 
combined with disciplined liability management. 
Pre-Provisioning Operating Profit surged 151% year-on-year to Rs. 201 crore, and 
up from Rs. 154 crore in the preceding quarter. 
Profit After Tax increased 140% year-on-year from Rs. 220 crore, and up from Rs. 96 
crore in Q1 FY27. 
This constant trajectory demonstrates that as we scale our lending franchise with a 
focus on risk-calibrated, secured assets, our operating model is delivering 
predictable, high-quality earnings growth. 
Moving on to our Payments vertical. 
Jio Payments Bank serves as a vital, high-frequency engagement layer across the 
entire group ecosystem. By capturing routine transaction velocity, it deepens 
customer stickiness and builds a natural cross-sell engine for our high-margin 
financial products. 
The bank saw strong operational execution that drove meaningful expansion in both 
our customer base and customer deposits. 
Our CASA customer base expanded 38% year-on-year to reach 40 lakh customers. 
This customer growth directly translated into strong deposit momentum, with total 
deposits growing 53% year-on-year to Rs. 643 crore. 
This underlying growth was further complemented by the expansion of our 
infrastructure-linked digital financial services. During the quarter, we expanded our 
toll operations footprint, which is now operational across 20 national highway toll 
plazas as well as 2 Multi-Lane Free-Flow barrierless toll plazas. 
9 

 
 
Consequently, our Total Income for the quarter grew 213% year-on-year to Rs. 94 
crore.  
During the quarter, we also received key regulatory approvals to launch our 3-in-1 
Savings Account as well as to act as ‘Banker to the Issue’ for public offerings, 
including IPOs, which will open up new revenue streams for the payments bank. 
Looking ahead, our strategic focus remains squarely on deepening customer 
stickiness and expanding high-margin fee streams. 
Moving on to Jio Payment Solutions.  
In this business, I would like to highlight our key product innovations that continue to 
strengthen our merchant value proposition. The new offerings launched during the 
quarter include contactless Tap-and-Pay on POS terminals for UPI and RuPay 
transactions and cross-border collection capabilities in over 100 currencies with T+2 
settlement for Indian exporters, among other solutions.  
Turning to our operating and financial metrics, our Total Payment Value for the 
quarter stood at Rs. 14,682 crore. As Hitesh mentioned earlier, the sequential 
movement in volume reflects our deliberate strategy to prioritize margin-accretive 
business. We are focused on ensuring that every transaction positively impacts both 
our top line and bottom line. Consequently, we chose to let go of certain 
high-volume, low-margin engagements, as our focus remains firmly on profitable 
growth rather than volume expansion alone. 
To drive profitable growth, we are actively pursuing high-margin segments, including 
small and medium businesses as well as exporters. 
As a direct result of this prudent customer mix and portfolio rationalization, our 
processing margins expanded significantly. Our net processing margin increased to 
14 basis points in Q2 FY27, up from 9 basis points in Q2 FY26 and 12 basis points 
in Q1 FY27.  
Correspondingly, Gross Fee and Commission Income reached Rs. 130 crore, while 
Net Fee and Commission Income grew 74% year-on-year to Rs. 21 crore. 
With the JioFinance app, we are reimagining what a financial services platform 
should look like for the future.  
Given what technology allows for today, and in line with the evolving needs of 
people, having a marketplace with the widest breadth of offerings is not enough by 
itself. Going forward, the moat in financial services is going to be owning the 
customer’s decision-making process. And that moat has to be built over time with 
10 

 
 
features that keep users engaged and guide them towards their financial well-being 
with trust, transparency and security.   
Earlier this year, we launched a major update to the JioFinance app, transforming it 
into a neural agentic marketplace powered by 50 AI agents and 10 machine learning 
models. This advanced architecture forms an intelligent, conversational layer that 
dynamically synthesizes customer data to deliver precise financial insights and 
personalized recommendations. 
Building on the intelligence and value-back propositions of the JioFinance app, we 
continue to expand our product suite, offering a comprehensive range of financial 
services.  
Today, our users have seamless access to an expansive suite of products, including 
71 credit card variants from 16 brands, 11 partner banks and NBFCs for personal 
loans, 7 deposit partners, and 94 insurance plans across 23 insurers. We have also 
recently expanded our offerings with the addition of JioSilver to our product suite. 
We recorded a 199% year-on-year rise in Jio Gold purchase transactions. Tax filings 
on the platform increased by 40% year-on-year, while Fixed Deposit Gross 
Merchandise Value grew by 50% quarter-on-quarter. 
While our Average Monthly Active Users stood at approximately 80 lakhs during the 
quarter—reflecting a temporary moderation in high-frequency, price-sensitive 
transaction volumes like digital gold due to external market conditions—our core 
user engagement continues to deepen significantly. 
During the quarter, we saw approximately 36,000 own and third-party products 
purchased daily across our digital platforms. Furthermore, our JioPoints loyalty 
program is yielding tangible cross-sell benefits: with 34 crore-plus points issued to 77 
lakh customers since launch, users engaged with JioPoints exhibit a 25% higher 
product-per-customer metric compared to the platform average.  
Complementing this intelligence is our integrated JioPoints rewards framework, 
which unifies everyday transactions into tangible savings. Customers earn JioPoints 
across routine in-app interactions and can redeem them across a wide network of 
over 110 premier partner brands. 
To further deepen customer engagement, we introduced two novel features on the 
app during the quarter—JioFinance+ and JioFinance360.  
JioFinance+ is a comprehensive membership program designed to deliver 
unmatched value across eligible marketplace products. Under its value-back model, 
a portion of the platform commission earned on eligible transactions is shared 
11 

 
 
directly with customers. Available complimentary for the first 365 days as an 
introductory offer, JioFinance+ offers tangible value through Assured Cash 
Valueback up to Rs. 5,000 on Personal Loans and up to Rs. 1,000 on Credit Cards, 
an extra 1% Jio Gold bonus on lump-sum purchases of Rs. 2,500 and above, and 
25% accelerated JioPoints across eligible transactions. 
Alongside this, JioFinance360 serves as an industry-first, complimentary financial 
health assessment platform. By combining Large Language Models with an 
intelligent rule-based engine, JioFinance360 consolidates fragmented assets and 
liabilities across multiple bank accounts, investments, loans, and insurance policies 
into a single, intuitive report. At its center is a personalized Financial Health Score, 
evaluated across five core pillars namely Spending, Borrowing, Wealth, Protection, 
and Tax. This equips users with actionable insights to eliminate spend leakages, 
address coverage gaps, and optimize tax planning. 
Together, these signature features form an intelligent engagement layer that 
enhances platform loyalty and positions JioFinance as a trusted, long-term financial 
companion. 
Our core strategic objective is to move beyond standard transaction facilitation by 
embedding smart, value-accretive tools directly into the customer journey. By offering 
proprietary capabilities that guide long-term financial health while rewarding routine 
usage, we deepen engagement across the customer lifecycle and increase customer 
lifetime value. 
With this, I would like to invite our Group Executive and Chief Financial Officer, Ms. 
Annapoorna Venkataramanan to discuss the progress across our Invest and Protect 
verticals followed by the financial performance for the quarter.

prepared in compliance with Indian Accounting Standards, as prescribed by the

Before getting into the numbers, I would like to set some context and look at how our 
operational outcomes align with our overarching long-term strategy. As a Core 
Investment Company, we build and nurture diverse businesses designed to serve 
four core customer needs: the need to borrow, transact, invest, and protect. 
Across all our operating entities, our business expansion continues to be 
underpinned by robust risk management frameworks, stringent compliance 
standards, and prudent liquidity management. As our entities hit critical mass, our
